Needs changes before merge. This is a safety review. Two paths can release incorrect machine moves without a warning.

The trial merge with upstream/main `fac6c8e8d22cb39bb0a4c18644b4ec1c4dbd2db6` was clean. All checks ran locally in a separate worktree. No GitHub runner was used.

Results:
- Build of the five selected test binaries: PASS.
- `camcraft-post`: `mach4_post` 3 passed; `mach4_trunnion` 3 passed; `script_mach4` 11 passed.
- `camcraft-app`: `mach4_builtin` 2 passed; `conformance` 7 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- Repeated mutations: disabled the RTCP guard, then disabled the simultaneous orientation guard. Each change made `mach4_refuses_rtcp_bad_trunnion_and_simultaneous_by_name` fail. Each restore made it pass. The post file now matches the reviewed head.
- Read all 14 new app NC goldens and all 11 new recorded verdicts line by line. No existing NC golden changed relative to current main.

Requested before merge:

1. **P1 — Set the initial rotary position before vertical cutting.** `assets/posts/mach4.cps:559` returns the vertical pose without setting A or C while `hasTilted` is false. The post also leaves the table at its last indexed angle at program end. I posted a vertical section followed by a section with stream orientation `A -45000 B 0 C 0`, on a non-RTCP AC table with X/Z rotary directions, zero pivots and offsets, and `table_rh` signs. The output starts with vertical XYZ cutting and no rotary position command. It later emits `G00 A-45. C-180.`, then ends with only a Z retract and M30. A repeat of this program starts its vertical cuts with the table still tilted. Retract and set the required initial rotary position on a configured trunnion before the first cut. Add a test for a repeated program that ends tilted.

2. **P1 — Restore the table position before a vertical probe section.** `assets/posts/mach4.cps:812` and the other probe hooks bypass `preparePose` and use untransformed coordinates. I added a probe tool change and a vertical GUARD/TOUCH section after the indexed section above. The post gave no warnings. After `G00 A-45. C-180.`, the probe section emits `G31 X10. Y5. Z10.` and `G31 X10. Y5. Z-5.` without a rotary reset. It then writes the result to G54. The probe therefore moves and measures in the wrong part orientation. Safely restore the vertical pose before these moves, or refuse this sequence by name. Add a test for indexed cutting followed by probing, including the offset update.

3. **P3 — Declare the supported post options.** `assets/posts/mach4.cps:301` reads `safeRetract`, `rolloverMode`, `rotaryUnclamp`, `rotaryClamp`, and `programNumber`, but the script has no `declaredOptions` schema. The normal CLI rejects the advertised setting:
   ```text
   post --option safeRetract=G53 assets/posts/mach4.cps <input.cnc> <output.nc>
   post: unknown post option 'safeRetract'
   ```
   The app also validates overrides against this schema. Declare the options with their types, defaults and valid values. Test them through the CLI or app option path. Direct `engine::run_with` calls do not check this path.

The issue discussion permits the current refusal of simultaneous cutting until #1966 is complete. The inherited UI test changes are already on current main; this trial merge adds no UI change that needs screenshots.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: the three findings in the latest review.

1. Initial rotary position. Configured AC trunnions retract and set both kinematic zero positions before initial vertical work. The pin is `mach4_repeated_program_indexes_vertical_before_first_cut`. It repeats a program that ends tilted and covers zero and nonzero rotary offsets. C-only machines retain their prior behavior.
2. Probing after indexing. Every probe hook restores the vertical pose through the retract/index guard before moves or offset writes. The pin is `mach4_indexed_cut_restores_vertical_before_probe_and_offset_update`. It checks GUARD, TOUCH, and the G54 update. It also catches a reset that incorrectly retains C at the vertical pole.
3. Supported options. The five options now declare types, defaults, and valid values. The pin is `mach4_cli_validates_declared_options_and_posts_overrides`. It exercises CLI overrides and rejects invalid values.

Each finding's mutation failed its pin. Each restore passed. The extra retained-C mutation also failed and restored green. Mach4 trunnion, recorded scripts, app builtin, and conformance passed. Clippy passed for camcraft-post and camcraft-app with all targets and warnings denied.

The required `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` completed all 581 steps. It is RED on 18 tests in six app suites: circular_pick_law, keep_law, kept_parts_live, pocket3d_open_side, stock_source_holes, and trochoid_law. All 18 failures reproduced on pristine upstream/main at fac6c8e8d22cb39bb0a4c18644b4ec1c4dbd2db6. Those failures were left outside this fix.

Current upstream/main was merged cleanly to use its option-validation API. New head: 29e169b81b1a6c5ab0ff0d11de0afb67b97ea451. The PR remains draft. Please re-review this head.

Needs changes before merge. This is a safety review. One probe approach can release an unsafe rapid move without a warning.

The three previous findings have fixes and passing tests:
- Initial vertical work sets both rotary zero positions after a safe retract. The test includes a repeated program and nonzero offsets.
- Probe hooks restore the vertical table position before probing and offset updates.
- The five options have a schema. The CLI test checks valid overrides and rejects invalid values.

Local results:
- The trial merge with upstream/main `3f41b8da6b65b8154132878e459d4430e3fb2063` has a code conflict in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`. Main moved `BUILTINS` to `posting_files.rs`. I aborted the trial merge. All builds and tests below ran on the PR head, not a merged tree.
- Build of the five selected test binaries: PASS.
- `camcraft-post`: `mach4_post` 3 passed; `mach4_trunnion` 6 passed; `script_mach4` 11 passed.
- `camcraft-app`: `mach4_builtin` 2 passed; `conformance` 7 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- I disabled initial rotary positioning. `mach4_repeated_program_indexes_vertical_before_first_cut` failed. It passed after restore.
- I disabled the probe pose reset. `mach4_indexed_cut_restores_vertical_before_probe_and_offset_update` failed. It passed after restore.
- I read the 14 new app NC goldens and 11 new recorded verdicts line by line. No existing NC or CL golden changed.
- The quick gate plan ran with `--dry-run`. I ran the five selected suites above, not the full gate. No GitHub runner was used.

Requested before merge:

1. **P1: Keep the first probe approach protected after a tool change or rotary reset.** `assets/posts/mach4.cps:852` calls `xyFirst` with `descend = true` and the previous stream position. After the retract and rotary reset, that position is stale. The call emits an unguarded rapid descent before the first `G31` move. The new probe regression fixture already emits `G00 Z0.` before `G31 ... Z10.`. I repeated it through the normal CLI. I then changed only the last indexed cutting endpoint from `Z 0` to `Z -10000`. The CLI succeeded without warnings and wrote:
   ```gcode
   G00 A0. C0.
   G00 Z25.
   G00 X10. Y5.
   G00 Z-10.
   G31 X10. Y5. Z10. F1200
   ```
   The probe can strike the part before contact detection is active. Establish the probe start position from the known retract state. Keep the descent protected, or refuse the sequence by name. Check `onProbeMove` at line 830 for the same call. Extend the regression test to check the approach moves, not only the rotary angles and offset update.

Notes:
- The source tree matches the reviewed head after both mutation restores.
- The PR changes no `crates/ui` files. No UI screenshots are required.
- The issue discussion permits refusal of simultaneous cutting until #1966 is complete.
- Keep `needs-rework` and `conflicts`. The draft must remain a draft while this finding is open.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: no findings fixed. The required merge hit the stop condition before changes were made.

The latest review requests one fix: protect the first probe approach after a tool change or rotary reset in onProbeGuard and onProbeMove. The regression must check the approach moves as well as rotary positioning and the offset update.

Merging upstream/main at 3c7385fba conflicts in crates/app/src/posting.rs at the BUILTINS declaration, near line 31. The PR adds Mach4 using include_str! to the embedded registry. Main replaces that registry with the posting_files.rs module and re-exports its file-backed BUILTINS. This is a refactor moving code edited by this branch. The resolve-conflicts skill explicitly requires stopping for that case. Resolving it would require carrying the Mach4 registration into the new registry.

I aborted the merge. No code, tests, labels, or draft status changed. No commit was pushed. Mutation checks, the quick gate, and clippy were not run. The head remains 29e169b81b1a6c5ab0ff0d11de0afb67b97ea451.

Please re-review the conflict hunk and provide direction on its resolution. The probe safety finding remains open.

Fixed the latest review's probe approach finding.

The first probe X/Y traverse now stays at clearance after a tool change or rotary reset. G31 protects the descent. onProbeGuard and onProbeMove no longer rapid to stale StartZ. The legacy onProbe hook uses the same protected approach.

The pin is `mach4_indexed_cut_restores_vertical_before_probe_and_offset_update`. It covers GUARD-first and direct TOUCH, with and without a tool change, after an indexed cut ending at Z-10. It checks approach moves, rotary reset, and the G54 update. Independently restoring each unsafe hook made the pin RED. Each restore was GREEN.

Merged upstream/main at 0a4a86ca1. Kept main's file-backed registry and added Mach4 to that registry and its browser fallback. Main's file-loading refusal tests and browser registry pin passed.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, all 589 steps. Clippy for camcraft-post and camcraft-app, all targets with warnings denied: GREEN. Selected Mach4 and app suites passed. No screenshots or review evidence were committed.

Needs changes before merge. This is a safety review. One probe positioning move can omit its contact alarm.

The previous findings have fixes and passing tests:
- Initial vertical work sets both rotary positions after a safe retract.
- Probe hooks restore the vertical pose before probing and offset updates.
- The CLI accepts the declared options and rejects invalid values.
- The first probe approach stays at clearance. G31 controls the descent instead of a rapid move to stale StartZ.
- The registry change preserves main's file loading and the browser fallback.

Local results:
- The trial merge with upstream/main `f887908f9901393d9aeb1356d5f8208e01bf0fbd` was clean. All checks below ran on that merged tree.
- Build of the five selected test binaries: PASS.
- `camcraft-post`: `mach4_post` 3 passed; `mach4_trunnion` 6 passed; `script_mach4` 11 passed.
- `camcraft-app`: `mach4_builtin` 2 passed; `conformance` 7 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- I restored the unsafe StartZ approach separately in `onProbeGuard` and `onProbeMove`. Each mutation failed `mach4_indexed_cut_restores_vertical_before_probe_and_offset_update` at an unguarded Z-10 descent. Each restore passed.
- I read all 14 new app NC goldens and all 11 new recorded verdicts line by line. No existing NC or CL golden changed.
- The quick gate plan ran with `--dry-run`. I ran the five selected suites above, not the full gate.
- The first build stalled with sccache and produced no artifacts. I stopped that build. The direct builds and checks passed with sccache disabled.
- No GitHub runner was used. No controller hardware test was done.

Requested before merge:

1. **P1: Check contact against the actual probe approach start.** `assets/posts/mach4.cps:856-859` still uses stream StartX/StartY/StartZ to select the guard checks. The new clearance approach can change that start. If the GUARD target equals the previous stream endpoint, the loop skips every check. The post then emits a real G31 descent with no positioning alarm.

   I reproduced this through the normal CLI with `assets/machines/3axis-vmc.mch`. The cutting section ends at `Feed X 10000 Y 5000 Z 10000 F 400000`. A probe tool change follows. ClearancePlane is 25. The probe section starts with `GUARD 10000 5000 10000 F 1200000`, then a Z TOUCH. The CLI succeeds without warnings and writes:
   ```gcode
   G00 Z25.
   G00 X10. Y5.
   G31 X10. Y5. Z10. F1200
   G31 X10. Y5. Z-5. F100
   IF[ABS[[#5063+5]]LT0.005]THEN#3000=2(PROBE NO CONTACT)
   ```
   There is no `PROBE HIT ON POSITIONING` check after the first G31. Contact above Z10 stops that move, but the next TOUCH can continue with the probe already in contact. Track the actual start after the clearance approach, or check each coordinate that the added approach changes. Add a regression where the stream endpoint equals the first GUARD target. Check the positioning alarm before the next probe move. Keep the passing approach tests.

Notes:
- The post file matches the reviewed head after both mutation restores.
- The PR changes no `crates/ui` files. No UI screenshots are required.
- The PR is mergeable. Remove the stale `conflicts` label and keep `needs-rework`.
- The draft must remain a draft while this safety finding is open.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: the latest review’s P1 probe positioning alarm finding.

GUARD now checks every commanded endpoint coordinate. It no longer skips the contact alarm when the stream endpoint equals the GUARD target but the clearance approach changes the actual start.

The pin is `mach4_cli_guard_checks_clearance_descent_when_stream_start_equals_target`. It runs the normal CLI on the three-axis VMC and indexed trunnion. It checks the clearance approach and the Z positioning alarm before the next TOUCH, followed by the offset update. The existing approach tests still pass. The Mach4 probe golden adds six positioning checks; moves are unchanged.

Reverting the post fix made the pin RED. Restoring it made all seven Mach4 trunnion tests GREEN. All eleven recorded Mach4 tests passed. `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 589 steps. Clippy passed for camcraft-post with all targets and warnings denied.

**Needs changes before merge.** This is a safety review (a new post writes G-code for a real machine). An agent that did not write the change did this review. The earlier `merge-ready` came from the author's own agents, so it is not an independent review (AGENTS.md "Only collaborators' reviews count").

### What looks good
- The provenance comment (`assets/posts/mach4.cps:1-4`) names public sources: the Mach4 Mill G-code manual and RS-274/NGC. I found no text that looks copied from a vendor post.
- Units come from `postOptions.Units` (G20/G21). The work offset comes from `PARAM WorkOffset` with `workOffsetIndex = true`, so the engine's `setup::wcs_slot` path stays the one source.
- The header states `G91.1`, and the arc output is incremental I/J/K from the absolute stream center (`IJKIncrement` is absolute per `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md:94`). The plane is restored before each cycle and at section end. Helical arcs write Z.
- The tool change writes M5, M9 and a safe retract, then `T.. M6` and `G43 H..`. The first traverse goes to the clearance plane first. The end writes M9, M5, a safe retract and M30.
- Tilted records on a machine without an AC trunnion, `rtcp = true`, a bad trunnion, travel limits and simultaneous moves are refused by name. A canned cycle without a feed is refused by name (`mach4.cps:784`). An unknown cycle type is refused by name (`mach4.cps:782`).
- The registry line is in `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` with its embedded fallback. No existing golden changed. Tests are in the correct crates. No new crate dependency.

### Results (merged with main `94f7d6b89`, built locally, Windows)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-post --test mach4_post` | 3 passed |
| `camcraft-post --test mach4_trunnion` | 7 passed |
| `camcraft-post --test script_mach4` | 11 passed |
| `camcraft-post --test g83_dwell` | 7 passed |
| `camcraft-post --test cycle_hop` | 7 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test conformance` | 7 passed |
| `camcraft-app --test mach4_builtin` | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

The trial merge had no conflicts. The changed files have no CR bytes.

### Requested before merge
1. **A cycle dwell is dropped with no message.** `assets/posts/mach4.cps:804` writes no P on G73 and G84. A PECK or TAP cycle with `P > 0` posts with no dwell and no diagnostic. This is the defect class of #2348 and #2354. Fix: before the cycle block, refuse a dwell on G73 and G84 by name, for example `canned cycle G73 cannot write a dwell on Mach4`. Add a test for each branch.
2. **P is written on cycles whose published Mach4 format has no P.** `assets/posts/mach4.cps:804` writes P on G83, G85 and G86. The formats in the public Mach4 Mill G-code manual list P only on G82 and G89 (G83 `X Y Z R Q F`, G85 and G86 `X Y Z R F`). The control can ignore the word, so the machine dwell can differ from the user's setting. This is the defect class of #2349. Fix: write P only on G82 and G89. Refuse a dwell on the other cycles by name, or cite a public Mach4 source for each cycle that you keep. Change the assertion at `crates/post/tests/mach4_post.rs:126` (G86 with `P0.25`) to match.
3. **The dwell unit has no cited source.** The post writes P in seconds (`mach4.cps:804`, `trimDec(secDwell, 3)`). The public Mach4 manual is not consistent: its glossary says seconds, but the G86 and G89 descriptions in one edition say milliseconds. Fix: in `docs/decisions/1968-mach4-post.md`, name the manual section and edition that you follow for the unit. Also say what the operator must set if the control reads P in milliseconds.

### Questions and notes (not blocking)
- `mach4.cps:803`: a PECK or DEEP cycle without a positive Q writes G73 or G83 with no Q. The control then uses a modal Q or gives an alarm. Do you want to refuse it by name, as the cycle feed is refused?
- `mach4.cps:796`: the cycle signature includes the dwell, so a dwell change writes G80 and a new full block. Good. When a G89 dwell goes to zero, the new G89 has no P. The manual format shows P as part of G89. Think about writing `P0` there, or using G85.
- `mach4.cps:875-876`: the G10 L2 update reads the active offset (`wcsIndex`) but writes offset `SetWorkOffset + 1`. Fanuc does the same. Confirm that this is the intended result when the two numbers are different.
- The PR body says the post is registered in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`. The line is in `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`. The body also says `mach4_trunnion.rs` has 3 tests, but 7 tests ran.
- Not exercised here: a run on a Mach4 control or simulator.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: all three requested changes in the latest review.

1. G73 and G84 now refuse positive dwell by cycle name before emitting the cycle. The pin is `mach4_refuses_dwell_on_g73_and_g84_by_name`.
2. P is emitted only on G82 and G89. G83, G85, and G86 refuse positive dwell by name. The pin is `mach4_refuses_dwell_on_g83_g85_and_g86_by_name`. The existing G86 fixture now requires no P. Zero-dwell cases still emit all five cycles without P.
3. The decision file cites the official Version 1.0 (2014) manual, glossary page 3, G82 page 37, and G89 page 49 for seconds. It identifies the later edition's milliseconds wording and gives operator instructions for millisecond controls. The pin is `mach4_supported_cycle_dwells_use_seconds_on_g82_and_g89_only`.

Each of the five refusal branches failed its pin when disabled. Each restore passed. Changing seconds output to milliseconds also failed its pin and restored green.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 590 steps, zero failures. All Mach4 suites and conformance passed. `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN. No goldens, screenshots, logs, or review evidence were committed.
